page: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is a virtual server instance powered by AMD EPYC processors running on the QEMU hypervisor with x86_64 architecture. The instance is provisioned with 2 shared vCPUs operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is 4.0 GB of RAM, equating to roughly 1.95 GB per core. Storage is provided locally as an 80 GB NVMe SSD, and the configuration contains zero GPUs. Advanced instruction set extensions including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), AES, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2 are exposed to the guest system.

Benchmark results highlight strong single-thread execution alongside expected multi-core scaling limitations typical of a dual-core shared configuration. The server achieves an upper-quartile Geekbench single-core score of 1939.0 and a stress-ng single-core result of 3016.89. In contrast, multi-core metrics place in the bottom 25 percent across stress-ng (5938.68), Geekbench multi-core (3520.0), and PassMark CPU (5189.05). Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 46.06 GB/sec read and 52.18 GB/sec write, while cached memory bandwidth is comparatively constrained at 312.61 GB/sec. Static web throughput sits in the bottom decile at 2.69 GB/sec, while lightweight LLM prompt processing for small 135M models averages 467.3 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, cpx22 offers an economical resource footprint that delivers fast per-core instruction processing and fast NVMe block storage for entry-level workloads. Because the vCPUs are shared rather than dedicated, resource contention may impact sustained high-load multi-threaded scenarios. The instance is well matched for lightweight web services, small microservices, CI/CD runner tasks, small database instances, and general developer staging environments that do not require dedicated vCPU throughput or massive memory capacities.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx22 is a dual-core virtual server featuring AMD EPYC x86_64 architecture with 2 shared vCPUs clocked at 2.0 GHz and 4.0 GB of memory. The instance includes 80 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and operates without dedicated GPU hardware. CPU feature support encompasses AVX-512 vector instruction sets, AES, and SHA-NI cryptographic extensions. In performance testing, the instance exhibits strong single-core capabilities, registering Geekbench single-core scores of 1939.0 and stress-ng results of 3016.89. However, aggregate multi-core throughput and memory subsystems fall into lower percentiles due to the 2-vCPU ceiling and shared resource topology. The platform delivers cost-effective per-core compute paired with fast NVMe access, making it appropriate for lightweight web applications, low-volume databases, utility scripts, and staging environments.
